issue.author: analyst
issue.body:
**Need:** an organization decision (edge or read tier) so the evaluation owner cannot read the candidates' files before every judgement is pushed. It feeds objective item 2 ("Say whether DojoWorld's organization … should change") and builder's graph change.

**Records** (`diagnosis/README.md` O2, analyst f72e8b7):
- On dev, `organization.py` EDGES has ("tuner", "judge"), and ACCESS gives judge→tuner `collaborate`. Only tuner→judge is `release-only`.
- In N4 `dw_df49de2d8788`, judge turn db83de61 at 10:49:34, before any result existed, read `/hutian/tuner/world-config.json` and both `/hutian/tuner/candidates/cand-g2|cand-h4/world-config.json` (17–27 KB each: the full prompts, including cand-h4's "Claim ledger" and "Truthfulness and calibration" sections, effort high vs medium). N4's objective said the account of how the workers differ goes "to the diagnostician and the tuner, not to the judge". The graph did not keep it from the judge.
- The judge needs nothing from the tuner to judge: the candidate names come from the objective, and results come labelled from the task-setter. With the approver moving to coach (your bdc17f3), the judge no longer accepts the root either.

**Options (yours):** (a) judge→tuner `release-only`, with the tuner publishing no release with candidate files before the evaluation ends (that is the tuner's restraint, weaker); (b) drop the tuner–judge edge, since the judge reaches the tuner's material through coach if ever needed; (c) keep it and say why. I'd take (b).

**Waits on it:** builder's organization-graph change and the organization section of my diagnosis.
issue.title: N4's judge read both candidates' worker files before judging: the tuner–judge edge gives the evaluation owner the candidates

comments.author: architect
comments.body: Decision: (b), drop the tuner-judge edge; the judge asks through the coach if it ever needs the tuner's material. In organization/review.md 'Revisions' on architect main. Builder: graph change.

issue.author: analyst
issue.body:
**Need:** a decision on DojoWorld's approver (objective item 2: "Say whether DojoWorld's organization, including which position approves the release, should change"), and, if it changes, the organization graph and owner rule for builder's PR.

**What the records show** (details: `diagnosis/checks.md` K7 and K8 in analyst, commit 2e6c1ab):
- N4 `dw_df49de2d8788` was approved by `judge` (`dojoworld status` → `release.verification.approval.approver: judge`). On dev, `src/dojoworld/dojoworld/organization.py` has `SLOTS['approver'] = 'evaluation'`, so the position that judges also accepts its own judging. `owner_errors` only stops the candidate owner from owning evaluation or tasks.
- The three approval checks (put-back, judgements, runs in `checks.py`) are all met by the judge's own records. Nothing judges, from outside the judge, the things the checks miss: the decision rule, blinding order, calibration redo, reading discipline, or whether the put-back ran the kept worker. In N4 the comparison is judge prose. It recomputes, but the conclusion "keep cand-g2" comes from an incumbent-default rule with a difference (0.2) inside 2 SE (0.75), and its sign depends on the free score given to one failed run.
- K8 (pending confirmation): N4's config gave the evaluation owner `worlds-heldout` (`"for": ["tasks","evaluation"]`), which reads the worlds the held-out runs are made in. Blinding then rests on the judge's restraint, which contradicts organization.py's own docstring (#319).

**My recommendation (yours to decide):** the approver should be a position that neither judges nor makes candidates nor runs the held-out tasks. Of the present six, that is the `direction` owner (coach). Move `SLOTS['approver']` to `direction` and make `owner_errors` refuse an approver that also owns evaluation, tasks or candidate. Coach reads judge release-only today. It needs at least the judge's `evaluation/` and the task-setter's after-judging records to accept, so read tiers and edges may change with it. A new acceptance position is the alternative; it costs a seventh position.

**What waits on it:** builder's PR (organization graph and owner rule) and my diagnosis's organization section.
issue.title: N4's judge approved its own judging: organization finding for the approver decision

Details in organization/review.md ('Decision'), pushed to architect main. Builder: please reflect this in the organization graph/owner rule.

comments.author: analyst
comments.body:
One concern with the decision in `organization/review.md` (bdc17f3), on the read tiers. Today the coach reads the task-setter **release-only** (organization.py ACCESS). That is one of the four tiers that keep the held-out tasks away from the tuner and diagnostician, who are the coach's neighbors. If the coach reads the task-setter's repository in full, it reads `tasks/source/` and `tasks/blind/` from the round's start, before any candidate is made, and the held-out isolation then rests on the coach's restraint. That is the same pattern as K8.

Suggestion that keeps both: leave coach→task-setter release-only, and have the task-setter publish its after-judging records (label table, run index, calibration key, drift) as a release once every judgement is pushed. The coach reads that release. The approval check can require that the release exists and that its label table matches the hash published before the judging (K4). Coach→judge in full is harmless, because judge's repository holds only judgements and the blind copies, which exist only after the runs. Your decision. I've noted this in the diagnosis.

issue.body:
**Need:** a fix so that a put-back in a world of another domain shows its turns. DojoWorld's put-backs are always in another domain (hengworld in the trial, researchworld in N4/N5), so with v6 **K1 can never pass**.

**Reproduced** on trial-machine, read-only, with the v6 install (~/op6/kaitian-dojo-checks), on the v6b trial's put-back `hw_146e78ba2766` (home `~/op6/dojohome-b/dw_52d127943f05/worlds/tuner`):
- With the dojo definition bound, as the DojoWorld runner is: `world_usage.own(home, host.json+world_id)` → `{"source": null, "note": "the world has no record of its ledger yet"}`, with no `roles`.
- With the heng definition bound: `{"turns": 2, "roles": {"curator": {"turns": 1}, "steward": {"turns": 1}}, "source": "record", "as_of": 1792841725.6}`. The record (captured 11:35:25) existed before the refusal at 11:37:22.
- Cause: `observe/capture.py:57 directory()` validates the world id with `world_id_pattern()`, i.e. `current().prefix` (`dw`). `hw_…` fails and raises ValueError. `_record`/`own()` swallow it into a note, and `made()` then hands over `usage` without `roles`.
- `checks.kept_problems` then takes `'usage' in state` as "the record is there" and `turns.get('steward')` as 0, and says "steward took no turn in put-back world hw_146e78ba2766: the kept worker produced no output there" (v6b monitor-full l.1517, owed to the end).

**Two fixes, both small:**
1. kernel: in `execution/worlds.py: _config_and_usage`, compute usage with the made world's own definition bound (`state['definition']`; `definition.py` has the scoped/bind helpers at l.275-293), or make `capture.directory` accept any world id (`_ANY_WORLD`, as `made()` already does for listing);
2. domain: `kept_problems` should treat a `usage` without `roles` (`source: null`) as "cannot be seen yet: <note>", not as zero turns.

**Also:** in v6a (`dw_27fed645624e`), "curator took no turn in put-back world hw_c1ecafdd447a" is the same defect, not only operator's topic. Under v6 any position of a put-back in another domain reads as having taken no turn.
**Shows it fixed:** a put-back whose kept position took a turn passes K1, and one where it took none is refused, in a trial world.
issue.title: K1 still cannot pass: made() reads a made world's turns under DojoWorld's own world-id pattern, so a hengworld/researchworld put-back has 'no record' and reads as 'took no turn'

issue.body:
**Need:** a fix so that a correct put-back passes K1. operator's v2 trial `dw_7ce4dfccc63b` never showed one (operator#… record `trial/README.md` at operator 5e44d963; analyst#3).

**Cause 1 (certain, from the code at builder d89688a).**
- `checks.kept_problems` reads `state['worker_config']['roles']` and `state['usage']['roles']` of the put-back world (checks.py:95-96).
- The approval gets `state` from `release.made_worlds()`, i.e. `control/made-worlds.json`. The runner fills that from `execution/worlds.py: made()` (lines 937-961), which copies only `labels`, `continues`, `world_status` and `release`.
- So `running` is always `{}`, and every put-back gets "runs, for steward, a worker that differs … in: everything (the position has no worker there)". That is exactly the refusal the trial met twice (hw_2615d41cad5b, then the remade hw_a3e78ec6b40d; monitor-full.txt l.1185, l.1910). The test feeds `worker_config` directly (`.agents/tests/test-release-delivery.py:2039`), so it never exercised the runner's record.
- Fix: `made()` also carries, per role of each made world, the worker it runs (`worker_config.roles`) and its turn count. Turns come from the ledger or receipts, since `usage` is computed by `status` and may not be in host.json; check which.

**Cause 2 (certain, from N4's records).**
- The host record adds a `sha256` to each asset that the worker file did not carry. N4 rw_c3cb69258d92: `worker_config.roles.paper-repo.assets[0]` has `sha256: 88437e34…`, while `candidates/cand-h4/paper-repo.worker.json` has none. The text is identical.
- Plain `!=` therefore refuses a correct put-back with "differs in: assets". Compare after dropping host-added asset digests, or after adding the digest of each asset's files to the kept file.

**What shows it fixed:** a trial whose put-back runs the kept worker passes `kept_problems`, and one that runs another worker is refused naming the differing keys. The v3 trial is the place.
**Waits on it:** the passing case of objective item 4 (no qualifying approval has been shown on any version).
issue.title: K1's kept_problems can never pass: the runner's made-worlds record carries no worker_config or usage, and the host adds asset sha256

issue.body:
Analyse the DojoWorld world given you to read, and draft the objective of DojoWorld's next round.

The world: dw_df49de2d8788 (N4, a fresh world). It judged two trained versions of the paper-writing worker of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (the workers of its positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo), cand-g2 and cand-h4, on held-out tasks, and put the one it kept back into rw_313df9cf84a4. The research worlds its positions made are given to read too, and so are rw_313df9cf84a4 and the three held-out worlds N4's runs started from (rw_5c4743418b6b, rw_686e5b0bd6da, rw_e263f2a52297). N4 has ended and was approved; it ran a DojoWorld that refuses an approval until three evaluation records pass their checks. Its objective is a draft that an earlier KaiTianWorld round wrote, with its blanks filled in by the user, who also reworded the sentence naming the held-out papers to fit the new papers chosen; the user drove the world and changed its configuration on the way (`config history` shows each change). The same state root holds three small trial worlds the user ran before N4 (dw_bea18ea81dac, dw_b6ad7a8fc6e8, dw_b8d32a1f11d3); they are history. The user's own notes on these worlds are not given.

1. Can N4's approval and its judgements be trusted? Say for each, from the world's records, and why. What did the three approval checks stop, and what did they not stop? Diagnose every problem the world shows: its kind, its place and the records that show it.
2. Problems that the definition, the organization, a domain's implementation or the kernel could have stopped and did not: make each into something a position can check, a command, a gate or the world's physics, that refuses what does not qualify and says what is missing, not into more guide text. Say whether DojoWorld's organization, including which position approves the release, should change, and why; if it should, change it in the pull request, its organization graph with it. One pull request to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian-376, base dev; merging it is the maintainer's decision. Change nothing that only a worker did, and keep each change small. If there is nothing to change, say why.
3. Problems only in workers' behavior or in the objective: a draft objective for DojoWorld's next round, in your repository. The next round answers one question: is cand-g2, the worker N4 kept, better than the paper-writing worker that rw_313df9cf84a4 itself records for those positions? Its tasks and its measure must be able to tell the two apart. Say in it how a failed run is counted and how the round decides that it cannot tell them apart. The maintainer decides whether to run it.
4. Try the pull request on trial-machine: install it there, build its images, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh DojoWorld world with a tiny task, every position, the judging one included, on Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5 at low effort ($TRIAL_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), at most 40 executions and 3000 model seconds over the trial world and every world it makes. The trial shows each new check refusing an approval or judgement that should be refused, with the refusal saying what is missing, and passing one that qualifies. The pull request says what changed, which findings it answers and how the trial ended (the trial world's id, its release, and what was refused and what passed).

The worlds given you to read stay as they are.

issue.body:
Analyse the DojoWorld world given you to read, and draft the objective of DojoWorld's next round.

The world: dw_df49de2d8788 (N4, a fresh world). It judged two trained versions of the paper-writing worker of the research world rw_313df9cf84a4 (the workers of its positions paper-repo and internal-review-repo), cand-g2 and cand-h4, on held-out tasks, and put the one it kept back into rw_313df9cf84a4. The research worlds its positions made are given to read too, and so are rw_313df9cf84a4 and the three held-out worlds N4's runs started from (rw_5c4743418b6b, rw_686e5b0bd6da, rw_e263f2a52297). N4 has ended and was approved; it ran a DojoWorld that refuses an approval until three evaluation records pass their checks. Its objective is a draft that an earlier KaiTianWorld round wrote, with its blanks filled in by the user, who also reworded the sentence naming the held-out papers to fit the new papers chosen; the user drove the world and changed its configuration on the way (`config history` shows each change). The same state root holds three small trial worlds the user ran before N4 (dw_bea18ea81dac, dw_b6ad7a8fc6e8, dw_b8d32a1f11d3); they are history. The user's own notes on these worlds are not given.

1. Can N4's approval and its judgements be trusted? Say for each, from the world's records, and why. What did the three approval checks stop, and what did they not stop? Diagnose every problem the world shows: its kind, its place and the records that show it.
2. Problems that the definition, the organization, a domain's implementation or the kernel could have stopped and did not: make each into something a position can check, a command, a gate or the world's physics, that refuses what does not qualify and says what is missing, not into more guide text. Say whether DojoWorld's organization, including which position approves the release, should change, and why; if it should, change it in the pull request, its organization graph with it. One pull request to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian-376, base dev; merging it is the maintainer's decision. Change nothing that only a worker did, and keep each change small. If there is nothing to change, say why.
3. Problems only in workers' behavior or in the objective: a draft objective for DojoWorld's next round, in your repository. The next round answers one question: is cand-g2, the worker N4 kept, better than the paper-writing worker that rw_313df9cf84a4 itself records for those positions? Its tasks and its measure must be able to tell the two apart. Say in it how a failed run is counted and how the round decides that it cannot tell them apart. The maintainer decides whether to run it.
4. Try the pull request on trial-machine: install it there, build its images, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh DojoWorld world with a tiny task, every position, the judging one included, on Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5 at low effort ($TRIAL_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY), at most 40 executions and 3000 model seconds over the trial world and every world it makes. The trial shows each new check refusing an approval or judgement that should be refused, with the refusal saying what is missing, and passing one that qualifies. The pull request says what changed, which findings it answers and how the trial ended (the trial world's id, its release, and what was refused and what passed).

The worlds given you to read stay as they are.
